newsitem.title: DUBAI: Britain arranging medical exam for nurses in Saudi.
newsitem.headline: Britain arranging medical exam for nurses in Saudi.

text.p: British officials are trying to arrange for a doctor to examine two jailed nurses awaiting a Saudi court verdict in a murder trial, a spokesman at the British embassy in Riyadh said on Tuesday.

If the court finds them guilty of any charge, the case would go through an elaborate appeals system in the kingdom, which applies strict Islamic laws including beheading by the sword for murderers, drug smugglers and rapists.

"British officials are working on gaining access for a British doctor and an agreement has been given in principle," the spokesman told Reuters. He said no date had been set for the medical examination.

A Foreign Office spokesman in London said on Monday that Saudi Arabia had agreed to the checkup following British pressure for something to be done about the conditions in which Deborah Parry, 38, and Lucille McLauchlan, 31, were being kept in jail.

The two are charged with murdering 55-year-old Australian nurse Yvonne Gilford, whose body was found in her room at the King Fahd military medical complex in the eastern Saudi city of Dhahran in December.
The women say they are innocent of the murder of Gilford, who was stabbed 13 times, bludgeoned and suffocated, and have withdrawn confessions they said were made under duress.

According to Saudi law, the victim's immediate family -- her mother Muriel and brother Frank Gilford -- have authority to demand execution if the defendants are found guilty and the court rules the death penalty is appropriate. Frank Gilford has repeatedly said he prefers the maximum punishment.
Sources close to the case said a court ruling was expected within days, but diplomats said a verdict had not yet been reached.
The British embassy spokesman said the doctor being considered to examine the nurses was based in Saudi Arabia.
